commit.message:
fix: fit the site header to phone widths

The header was laid out as one unbreakable row. .site-nav was a shrinkable
flex item, so under pressure it gave way before the search box did: "Agent
tools" broke onto a second line and stretched all four links into a 60px row
inside a 56px header, and below 768px the rest ran off the right edge — 244px
of horizontal overflow at 375.

The nav is now flex: none with nowrap labels, so the search box is the element
that yields, and below 768px the header wraps to two rows with the nav taking
the second one whole. That keeps all four labels intact and on one line down to
320px; shortening "Agent tools" would have changed a primary nav label instead.
The TUHH wordmark is the one deliberate casualty on phones and returns at 768.

--hc-search-max is a new token for the same reason --hc-sweep is one: the rule
that consumes it is the last #search-form rule in the file, so a media query
earlier in the file cannot outrank it. --header-h is redefined with the phone
block because h1-h4 scroll-margin-top is measured from it.

Two adjacent overflow fixes on the same widths, both pre-existing and both one
line: .card-grid's 19rem track floor is wider than a 320px viewport (3px), and
search-result code paths had no break opportunity (274px).

Verified at 320/375/390/768 across eight routes and both themes: zero
horizontal overflow, nav on one line, toggle in view, anchors landing clear of
the header. The header search box still sweeps open leaving #/ and shut
returning to it, a cold deep link still paints it full size without animating,
and a zeroed --hc-sweep still collapses both to instant. check.py all green;
423 node tests and 341 python tests pass.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <redacted@example.invalid>

setup(raspberry-pi): complete the I2C boot config and say which bus is which

SETUP-PARITY R10 (register item 3.6, first half). The page gave only
dtoverlay=i2c4,pins_6_7, which yields /dev/i2c-4 alone.

Evidence:
- 02 (lab robot Pi, manifest captured 2026-08-17): config.txt lines 11, 13, 66
  carry dtparam=i2c_arm=on, dtoverlay=i2c6,pins_22_23, dtoverlay=i2c4,pins_6_7;
  i2c-buses.txt lists i2c-1, i2c-4, i2c-6, i2c-20, i2c-21.
- 03 (live probe 2026-08-19 15:25 CEST): same three lines at the same line
  numbers; ls /dev/i2c-* returns all five buses after a power cycle.
- Pin mapping for i2c4 matches the UUV pinout SVG (GPIO6 SDA4 / GPIO7 SCL4).
- 01: to be confirmed after its re-image (hippo-main-01 parity run 2026-09-16).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <redacted@example.invalid>

setup(raspberry-pi): add dtoverlay=uart3 to the UART page

SETUP-PARITY R11 (register item 3.6, second half). The UART page listed
uart2, uart4, uart5, while the Ubuntu 24.04 page lists uart2-uart5. The two
pages contradicted each other; the real machines follow the Ubuntu page.

Evidence:
- 02 (manifest captured 2026-08-17): config.txt lines 67-70 are
  dtoverlay=uart2, uart3, uart4, uart5.
- 03 (live probe 2026-08-19 15:25 CEST): config.txt lines 67-70 identical.
- The ttyAMA numbering depends on which UARTs are enabled (the page's own
  note), so the missing uart3 also shifted the device numbers.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <redacted@example.invalid>

setup(raspberry-pi): expected output shows fcu_data, not fcu_tele

SETUP-PARITY R14 (register item 3.7, first half). Both pages print
/dev/fcu_tele in the expected `ls /dev/fcu*` output, but the 50-serial.rules
the UART page gives creates fcu_data for uart5, and the PX4 page then uses
`MicroXRCEAgent serial --dev /dev/fcu_data`. No rule anywhere creates fcu_tele.

Evidence:
- 02 (manifest captured 2026-08-17): udev-rules.d/50-serial.rules line 6
  creates SYMLINK+="fcu_data"; byte-identical to the rule on the UART page.
- 03 (2026-08-19 15:28 CEST): the same rule installed (sha256 564a84bc...);
  fcu_tele appears nowhere on the machine.
Only the name changed. The ttyAMA numbers stay as printed; the page's note
already says they depend on which UARTs are enabled.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <redacted@example.invalid>

setup(getting-started): point mavlink-router at /dev/fcu_usb

SETUP-PARITY R48 (register item 3.7, second half). The example main.conf
used Device =/dev/ttyACM0, while the USB Configuration page creates the
stable name /dev/fcu_usb for exactly this device, and the FCU firmware page
says to choose /dev/fcu_usb. ttyACM0 breaks silently as soon as a second
USB-serial device is attached.

Evidence:
- 02 (manifest captured 2026-08-17): udev-rules.d/50-fcu.rules line 3
  (vendor 26ac, product 0012) creates SYMLINK+="fcu_usb".
- 03 (2026-08-19 15:28 CEST): the same rule installed, sha256 e7ea8762...
- Not verified: 02's own main.conf was never captured, and no FCU was
  attached to 03, so the running router was not exercised.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <redacted@example.invalid>

setup(raspberry-pi): install chrony at first boot and explain the clock trap

SETUP-PARITY R29 (register item 3.3). The Pi setup path never mentions time,
although a Pi has no RTC and a wrong first-boot clock makes apt refuse every
repository. The chrony page existed but nothing on the Pi path linked to it.

Evidence:
- 02 (manifest captured 2026-08-17): chrony 4.5-1ubuntu4.2 installed and
  enabled (dpkg-versions.tsv, systemd-enabled.txt).
- 03 (2026-08-19 15:26 CEST): chrony 4.5-1ubuntu4.2, clock correct.
- The failure really happened on 03's first boot (2026-08-17, MIGRATION.md
  §4a Trap 1): clock read 2026-02-10, apt exited 100, cloud-init ended with
  status: error and installed none of its packages; re-running after the
  clock synced worked unchanged.
- 03 (2026-08-19) and 01 (2026-09-16, still Raspbian): both report no RTC.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <redacted@example.invalid>

setup(raspberry-pi): document the unattended-upgrades dpkg-lock wait

SETUP-PARITY R31 (register item 3.4). No page mentioned unattended-upgrades,
the dpkg frontend lock, or apt's lock timeout. Killing the upgrade to get the
lock back is the one mistake here that costs a re-image.

Evidence:
- 03 first boot (2026-08-17, MIGRATION.md §4a Trap 2): unattended-upgrade ran
  about 120 packages including the kernel for over 30 minutes and held
  /var/lib/dpkg/lock-frontend; pgrep unattended-upgrade returned nothing.
- 03 /var/log/apt/history.log (read 2026-08-19): 68 consecutive
  /usr/bin/unattended-upgrade transactions between 14:25 and 14:57 on 08-17.
- 03 (2026-08-19 15:26-15:29 CEST): every apt call used
  -o DPkg::Lock::Timeout=3600 and completed; dpkg --audit stayed empty.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <redacted@example.invalid>

setup(getting-started): install the ROS 2 apt source with ros2-apt-source

SETUP-PARITY R03 (register item 3.5). The page hand-rolled a ros2.list and
fetched the key from rosdistro. The lab's robot Pis use the official
ros2-apt-source package instead, which owns both the key and a deb822
ros2.sources file.

Evidence:
- 02 (manifest captured 2026-08-17): no ros2.list; ros2.sources is a symlink
  to /usr/share/ros-apt-source/ros2.sources; ros2-apt-source 1.2.0~noble.
- 03 (2026-08-19 15:25 CEST): same symlink, ros2-apt-source 1.2.0~noble,
  no ros2.list (installed that way on 2026-08-17, MIGRATION.md Step 9).
- 2026-09-16: the release lookup returns 1.3.0 and the resulting
  ros2-apt-source_1.3.0.noble_all.deb URL answers HTTP 200.
- 01: to be installed this way after its re-image and recorded in
  HIPPO-01-SETUP.md.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <redacted@example.invalid>

setup(concepts): query the package list for the local architecture and refresh it

SETUP-PARITY R04 and R05 (register item 3.8). The page hard-coded the amd64
index and printed a 20-entry list, while the live index serves 28 and the
Tip names meta-packages (hippo_full, hippo_robot) the printed list lacked.
A Pi reader copying the command got the amd64 answer for an arm64 machine.

Evidence (read live 2026-09-16 from repositories.hippocampus-robotics.net,
Release dated Fri, 29 Aug 2025 15:17:34 UTC):
- binary-amd64/Packages: 28 packages (the list now printed).
- binary-arm64/Packages: 27 packages; the only difference is
  ros-jazzy-acoustic-msgs. binary-all: HTTP 404.
- ros-jazzy-hippo-robot 1.0.3-0noble Depends includes ros-jazzy-acoustic-msgs
  (R06); 03 (2026-08-19 15:27 CEST) proved it with apt-get -s install:
  "Depends: ros-jazzy-acoustic-msgs but it is not installable".
- 02 (manifest 2026-08-17) is aarch64 (hardware-and-os.txt line 14).
Also fixes the install example, which was missing `sudo apt install`.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <redacted@example.invalid>

setup(raspberry-pi): replace the inert ifupdown Ethernet hook, marked untested

SETUP-PARITY R32 (register item 3.9). The page's fix ran $ETHTOOL, a variable
that only ifupdown hooks receive. Ubuntu 24.04 Server, which the same section
tells you to flash, uses netplan and systemd-networkd, so the hook never runs.

Evidence:
- 02 (manifest captured 2026-08-17): ifupdown not installed
  (dpkg-versions.tsv has no entry); networking is cloud-init netplan, eth0 DHCP.
- 03 (2026-08-19 15:25 CEST): dpkg -l ifupdown -> "un ifupdown <none>";
  /etc/network/if-pre-up.d/ exists but nothing executes it; the documented
  hook file was never created.
The replacement calls ethtool directly (now, and from a oneshot unit at boot).
It is labelled untested: nobody has reproduced the lag it is meant to fix,
and it was not run on 01 or 03 because it renegotiates the link the SSH
session depends on.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <redacted@example.invalid>

setup(raspberry-pi): document the wifi/Bluetooth disable overlays and the lock-out risk

SETUP-PARITY R33 (register item 3.10, first part). No page mentioned
dtoverlay=disable-wifi or disable-bt, which the lab's robot Pis carry. With
both, Ethernet is the only way in, so the warning belongs next to the lines.

Evidence:
- 02 (manifest captured 2026-08-17): config.txt lines 41-43
  "# disable bluetooth and wifi", dtoverlay=disable-wifi, dtoverlay=disable-bt;
  line 30 enable_uart=1.
- 03 (2026-08-19 15:25 CEST): config.txt lines 42-43 identical.
- HANDOFF-REPORT.md item 7: the first post-flash outage on 03 was a dead
  Ethernet cable that looked like a permanent loss of access.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <redacted@example.invalid>

setup(lab-cameras): install the iniVation and uhubctl udev rules

SETUP-PARITY R35 (register item 3.10, second part). The event-camera page
never mentions a udev rule for either the camera or uhubctl, which is why its
uhubctl commands need sudo. The lab's robot Pi carried both rules.

Evidence:
- 02 (manifest captured 2026-08-17): udev-rules.d/65-inivation.rules (DVS/DAVIS
  vendor/product rules, MODE 0666, GROUP video/plugdev) and
  udev-rules.d/50-uhubctl.rules ("for rootless operation on Linux for users in
  group dialout").
- 03 (2026-08-19 15:28 CEST): both installed, sha256 65f0d7db... and
  accc1651..., identical to 02's.
- 2026-09-16 upstream: libcaer_driver's README says to copy
  65-inivation.rules into /etc/udev/rules.d and add the user to video and
  plugdev; mvp/uhubctl ships udev/rules.d/52-usb.rules, a newer revision of the
  file 02 installed as 50-uhubctl.rules (same rules, DRIVER now "hub|usb").
Not verified: rootless uhubctl on a lab Pi; stated as the rule's intent.

R49 (the 24.04 route for the iniVation software) needs no change here: this
page already builds libcaer from source via libcaer_driver's vcs import.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <redacted@example.invalid>

- 03 (2026-08-19 15:25 CEST): no hippo_core under /home/pi/ros2/src.
- 2026-09-16: HippoCampusRobotics/hippo_common has scripts/build-ros,

setup(raspberry-pi): say chrony cannot prevent the first-boot clock failure

SETUP-PARITY R29 and R31 (register items 3.3 and 3.4), follow-up with new
evidence from the hippo-main-01 re-image.

Evidence, hippo-main-01, Ubuntu 24.04.4 arm64, 2026-09-16:
- cloud-init user-data listed chrony under packages:. First boot still ended
  with cloud-init status: error. /var/log/cloud-init-output.log: apt-get update
  "Release file ... is not valid yet (invalid for another 218d 7h 47min)", i.e.
  the clock read the image date (2026-02-10). None of the packages installed,
  chrony included, so listing it cannot prevent the failure.
- The follow-on install in the same run failed with "404 Not Found" on
  noble-updates packages, because apt still used the image's old lists.
- systemd-timesyncd synchronized the clock by itself (timedatectl:
  System clock synchronized: yes). apt-get update, then the same installs,
  succeeded unchanged (01 run log, 15:32 CEST).
- During apt-get upgrade (openssh-server upgraded), new SSH connections to 01
  were refused from about 15:36 to 15:40 CEST while ping kept answering; SSH
  came back by itself when apt finished the package.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <redacted@example.invalid>

setup(raspberry-pi): the stock image already enables i2c_arm; add only the overlays

SETUP-PARITY R10 (register item 3.6), follow-up to 0d6ccd2 with the stock
config.txt as evidence.

Evidence:
- Ubuntu 24.04.4 preinstalled server arm64 image (sha256 790652fa...0d37,
  Canonical SHA256SUMS), its system-boot config.txt saved by flash-01.sh on
  2026-09-16: line "dtparam=i2c_arm=on" sits in the base section before any
  dtoverlay=, and "enable_uart=1" is present too (the fallback that c25803c's
  warning relies on is stock).
- diff of that stock file against hippo-main-02's config.txt (rootfs-02,
  sha256 4f106dd3...1866): 02 adds only dtoverlay=i2c6,pins_22_23 (after the
  stock dtparam), the disable-wifi/-bt pair, and dtoverlay=i2c4,pins_6_7 plus
  uart2..uart5 at the end. No second dtparam=i2c_arm line.
- hippo-main-01 booted with 02's file on 2026-09-16: ls /dev/i2c-* lists
  i2c-1, i2c-4, i2c-6, i2c-20, i2c-21, as the page says.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <redacted@example.invalid>
proposal: drop derived files (derive.yml regenerates them after merge)

proposal: re-sync the derived search files with main

Mechanical only: search/manifest.json and search/site.json are derived outputs
(CLAUDE.md: never committed in a pull request; derive.yml regenerates them on
main). main has moved since 825bab4, so the branch's copies conflicted. They now
match origin/main byte for byte. No content decision on this proposal was made
or changed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <redacted@example.invalid>

proposal: merge main (75f09dd) and stop carrying the derived search files

Mechanical only. No word of this proposal's prose was changed, added or removed,
and nothing main did was reverted.

Why: this is the second time the pull request went stale. Every push to main runs
derive.yml, which commits fresh search/manifest.json and search/site.json; a branch
that carries its own copies of those files conflicts the moment that happens. The
2026-09-23 fix only re-synced the copies, so the wound reopened five commits later.

The durable fix is for the branch to stop differing from main on those two files at
all, which is what CLAUDE.md's edit map asks for ("Derived outputs ... never
committed in a pull request; derive.yml commits them on main"). Both conflicted here
and both are resolved to origin/main's exact bytes, so the pull request's diff no
longer touches them. CI regenerates them with tools/derive.py in the workspace before
running the gate, so the proposal does not need its own copies.

The two content files main also edited, content/setup/concepts/colcon.md and
content/setup/raspberry-pi/uart-configuration.md, auto-merged with no conflict: the
edits are in different places. main's typo fixes ("environment", "KERNELS
parameter") and this proposal's own edits are both present in the merged result.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <redacted@example.invalid>

+### udev Rule
+
+Without a udev rule only root can open the camera. The driver's [README](https://github.com/ros-event-camera/libcaer_driver/) asks you to copy iniVation's `65-inivation.rules` (it ships with the libcaer source that `vcs import` fetched) and to add your user to the `video` and `plugdev` groups:
+
+```console
+$ sudo cp $WS_DIR/libcaer/lib/udev/rules.d/65-inivation.rules /etc/udev/rules.d/ \
+&& sudo usermod -aG video,plugdev $USER \
+&& sudo udevadm control --reload-rules && sudo udevadm trigger
+```
+
+If the file is not at that path, search for it with `find $WS_DIR -name 65-inivation.rules`. Log out and back in so the new groups apply.
+
 ### Repower USB

 && sudo make install

Attention

+ +A Raspberry Pi has no battery-backed clock. On the first boot the system time can be months in the past. apt then rejects every repository as "not valid yet", and cloud-init finishes with `status: error` without installing its `packages:`. This is not a broken image. Listing `chrony` under `packages:` does not prevent this, because `chrony` is one of the packages that fail to install.
